mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC, increasing from -31.0% to -28.1% in the last week, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity, which will continue to drive retail and recreation mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite the observed upward movement from t-1w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, evidenced by the consistent week-on-week increases and now reaching -21.6% from baseline, signals a return of commuting routines that will lift weekday retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains above -22% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days in more than 50% of instances where WORKPLACES remained above -22% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined and sustained recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, with both series showing consistent week-on-week increases, indicates a broader return to pre-pandemic routines, which will synergistically boost retail and recreation activity, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing their recovery trends (i.e., becoming less negative).

mechanism_narrative: In a 'reopening' regime, a recent dip in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 13.4% to 12.1% suggests people are spending less time at home and more time out, which will translate into increased RETAIL_REC over the next one week as they seek out external activities.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 7 days, even if RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline by more than 1 percentage point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a minor recent uptick, RETAIL_REC remains significantly below its pre-pandemic baseline, indicating persistent behavioral shifts away from non-essential outings and a general cautiousness, which will keep retail and recreation mobility lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the persistent low baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Fluctuations in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, particularly if it drops below 0% from baseline again after its recent rise, indicate a general cautiousness in public movement that will negatively impact discretionary retail and recreation, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days, even if GROCERY_PHARM drops below 0% from baseline for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The strong rebound in PARKS mobility (from -34.9% to -23.1%) combined with the recent dip in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 13.4% to 12.1%) suggests a significant shift towards outdoor and out-of-home activities, which will indirectly benefit retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days, despite PARKS maintaining its rebound and RESIDENTIAL remaining below 12.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a 'tightening restrictions' regime, the current slow recovery of WORKPLACES mobility, remaining significantly below -20% from baseline, indicates a lack of impetus for broader economic activity and a reluctance for in-person work, which will prevent RETAIL_REC from improving over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, even with WORKPLACES remaining below -20% from baseline in a tightening restrictions regime.
